codeReview.summary: The feature successfully deleted all 12 listed legacy agent files, removed the _LegacyAgentRuntime class, cleaned runtime/agent/__init__.py, and rewired/deleted corresponding test files. The full validation suite (make test, make lint, make typecheck, make format) passes. However, several stale documentation and docstring references to deleted modules were left untouched in scaffold files, backend AGENTS.md, and one source docstring.

issues.description: Module docstring still references deleted module: 'Session/history helpers for :mod:`fleet_rlm.runtime.agent.chat_agent`.' The chat_agent.py file was deleted; docstring should reference FleetAgent or AgentRuntime instead.

Backend agent instructions reference deleted files: 'Keep the main cognition loop in `runtime/agent/chat_agent.py` and `runtime/agent/recursive_runtime.py`'. Both files were deleted as part of this feature. This misleads future AI agents working on the backend.
Scaffold documentation references deleted RLMReActChatAgent class and deleted runtime/agent/chat_agent.py path. Scaffold files are curated packaged guidance and should be kept accurate.
Scaffold documentation references deleted runtime/agent/chat_agent.py file and RLMReActChatAgent class.
Scaffold documentation references deleted RLMReActChatAgent and deleted test categories (chat turns, recursion, delegation, routing).
Scaffold documentation contains an actual dangling Python import example: `from fleet_rlm.runtime.agent.chat_agent import RLMReActChatAgent`. Both the module and class were deleted.

`_TRANSCRIPT_OUTPUT_DEFAULTS` dict contains dead entries for 'reflect-and-revise' and 'context-selection' module slugs. The corresponding optimizer modules (optimize_reflect_and_revise.py, optimize_recursive_context_selection.py) and their DSPy module classes were deleted, so these entries are unreachable dead code.
`_ASSISTANT_SINKS` dict contains dead entries for 'reflect-and-revise' and 'context-selection' module slugs. Same issue as above — unreachable dead code since the modules no longer exist.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend AGENTS.md (src/fleet_rlm/AGENTS.md) contains stale runtime ownership guidance referencing deleted files (runtime/agent/chat_agent.py and runtime/agent/recursive_runtime.py). This file is actively consumed by AI agents and should be updated when files are deleted.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Scaffold SKILL.md files under src/fleet_rlm/scaffold/ contain curated code examples and references that were not updated after legacy deletions. The mission AGENTS.md says scaffold files should be updated directly, but there is no explicit checklist item reminding workers to grep scaffold/ for stale references after deleting source modules.

Docstrings in surviving modules (e.g., chat_session_state.py) were not updated after the module they describe (chat_agent.py) was deleted. The mission AGENTS.md does not remind workers to grep for docstring references to deleted modules.

The backend-refactor skill was followed correctly for the core deletion and rewiring work. The worker ran the required validation suite and all checks passed. The only deviation was not cleaning scaffold and AGENTS.md stale references, which are arguably outside the 'executable code' scope but still within src/fleet_rlm/.

The session_history.py file was moved from runtime/agent/ to runtime/execution/ rather than deleted. This was the correct choice because it is still imported by execution drivers, but the feature description and validation contract both list it as a file to delete. Workers may need guidance that 'delete from runtime/agent/' can mean 'move to a more appropriate location' when the module is still used.

summary: The delete-legacy-agent-files feature is functionally complete and safe to merge. All 12 targeted legacy files are removed from runtime/agent/, _LegacyAgentRuntime is gone, __init__.py exports only surviving symbols, test files are cleaned, and the full validation suite passes. Eight non-blocking issues remain: stale docstrings, stale scaffold SKILL.md examples, a stale backend AGENTS.md reference, and unreachable dead entries in transcript_exports.py. None affect runtime behavior, but they should be cleaned in a follow-up chore commit to prevent misleading future developers and AI agents.
